messages:
Marta K.: FYI NorthStar (enterprise) just sent final ask for Q3 dedicated commit in eu-west-1: they want 1200 GPUh/week sustained with a 20% burst window. Can we fit that without breaking other commitments?
Raj P.: quick status: current reserved dedicated pools in eu-west-1 are 1600 GPUs total, of which ~78% already reserved for other customers and internal use. That leaves ~352 GPUs nominally, but we need to convert to GPU-hours/week.
Olivia C.: Convert: one A100-80GB equiv GPU * 168h = 168 GPUh/week. So 352 GPUs * 168h = 59,136 GPUh/week — that's raw capacity but most are multi-tenant and not available for dedicated splits. Need to look at pinned node counts not raw inventory.
Liam S.: For contract talks, NorthStar's asks are normalized to 'A100-equivalent GPU hours'. They expect consistent latency SLO (p95 < 200ms) — implies dedicated placement not noisy neighbors.
capacity-bot: AUTO-CALC: if we allocate 1200 GPUh/week dedicated -> ~7.14 GPU sustained (1200 / 168). With 20% burst = 1440 GPUh/week -> ~8.57 GPUs sustained.
Marta K.: So they effectively want a 9-GPU pool in eu-west-1 with burst rules. Do we have that headroom after existing Dedicated contracts?
Raj P.: Not without reshuffling. Our current Dedicated commitments in eu-west (pinned) total 62 GPUs pinned across customers. Free pinned capacity (unallocated) is 2 GPUs. We can create ephemeral capacity via shared pool but that breaks their SLO unless we guarantee affinity.
Olivia C.: Options: 1) Offer 9 pinned GPUs for the commit but they'd be from new infra purchases or reassigning from low-util customers (painful). 2) Offer 7 pinned GPUs + 20% burst from shared pool with a contractual fallback to hosted region (us-west-2) if burst not satisfied. 3) Offer 7 pinned GPUs + autoscale to 9 with higher burst billing (1.5x).
Liam S.: NorthStar prefers single-region eu-west for data residency. Cross-region fallback likely a dealbreaker unless we can guarantee encryption and latency SLAs.
Dan (CS): They also have higher load forecast for November (seasonal campaign) — they said +40% peak for 3–4 weeks. That needs to be included in sizing or a known burst plan.
Raj P.: Let's run through weekly GPU-hour math including seasonal bump. Baseline ask: 1200 GPUh/wk. Seasonal peak (+40%) -> 1680 GPUh/wk. With 20% contract buffer already folded in? If buffer applied after season: 1680 * 1.2 = 2016 GPUh/wk -> ~12 GPUs pinned (2016 / 168 = 12).
Marta K.: That's a big delta. We need to show cost impact to sales. Can someone sketch a quick cost delta for 12 pinned GPUs vs 7 pinned + burst?
capacity-bot: COST-ESTIMATE (rough): pinned GPU monthly price (infra cost) = $2,800/GPU/month => weekly ~ $700/GPU. 12 GPUs -> $8,400/week -> ~$36,400/month. 7 GPUs pinned -> $4,900/week; burst hours billed at 1.5x at 5 GPUs equivalent during peak weeks (estimate) -> additional ~ $3,750/week when bursting.
Olivia C.: Also remember networking: eu-west egress charges and intra-region cross-AZ capacity can create steering constraints. If we pin 12 GPUs across two AZs, we must ensure they live in same AZ for latency-critical workloads. That reduces available inventory further.
Raj P.: Operational risk: if we promise 12 pinned GPUs in eu-west-1 but our hardware lead time is 8–10 weeks, procurement timing matters. Can Sales accept a phased commit? e.g., 7 pinned immediately, rest online by start of November?
Liam S.: Sales says NorthStar wants full Q3 coverage from day 1 of contract (Sept 1). They have marketing-driven spikes in Nov, but Q3 they expect baseline 1200/wk. They might accept phased if we give credits for shortfall.
Dan (CS): Also negotiation lever: offer a smaller committed baseline with a predictable burst SLA (guaranteed burst windows) at a premium. Many customers accept burst rate instead of large upfront commit.
Marta K.: Proposed internal recommendation: offer option A (9 pinned GPUs / 1440 GPUh/wk) — meets baseline + 20% buffer but not seasonal spike; option B (7 pinned + burst up to 12 for seasonal weeks, burst priced at 1.75x) — lower base cost, operationally feasible; option C (12 pinned, starts Nov 1, with credits for Sep/Oct) — highest cost, meets all peaks but requires procurement. Thoughts?
Raj P.: From infra risk POV, B is safest: we don't need new HW purchases immediately, we use shared pool + burst policy, but must document degraded SLO behavior if affinity can't be satisfied. Also add a runbook for cross-customer eviction ordering and preemption.
Olivia C.: If we go B, we need to lock scheduling knobs: max-burst-concurrency, burst-rate, and pre-empt-priority tag for the pool. Example config snippet we can give sales: ```
placement: dedicated
pinned_gpus: 7
burst: {
  enabled: true,
  max_additional_gpus: 5,
  billing_multiplier: 1.75,
  guarantee_window: "15m"
}
fallback: hosted_eu_pool (best-effort)
```
Liam S.: Sales can present B as cost-saving and predictable: show monthly comparison and an add-on for guaranteed burst windows at extra cost. NorthStar can choose C if they prioritize predictability.
Dan (CS): Also flag a hard limit: if they want cross-AZ pinned set, price +20% to cover AZ affinity constraints.
Marta K.: OK next steps: Raj/Olivia to produce a short infra feasibility note with exact pinned inventory per AZ and procurement ETA for additional GPUs, including cost table. Liam/Dan to draft commercial options A/B/C and pricing. I'll loop in Finance for margin checks. Target: share with NorthStar by EOD Friday.
Raj P.: Will do — I'll pull AZ-level pinned counts and confirm whether we can shuffle 2 GPUs from low-util accounts to create the 7 pinned immediately.
Olivia C.: I'll draft the burst config + runbook and estimate the network egress impact.
Liam S.: I'll prep the commercial options and highlight the seasonal clause and credit terms.
Dan (CS): I'll prep a short note about customer expectations for single-region residency and propose language for acceptable fallback.
capacity-bot: NOTE: ticket created infra/allocations #4832 tracking this request (link: https://redwood.internal/infra/allocations/4832).
Marta K.: Thanks team :thumbsup:
